prompt: A beacon that lights up when any rover is within 20 metres.

request_messages.content: A beacon that lights up when any rover is within 20 metres.

answer.text:
Love it: a beacon that wakes up when a rover comes close is a great building block for a camp. Two details are worth deciding first, because Mars has opinions about both.

**1. What keeps it lit at night?** Sunlight at the top of Mars' atmosphere averages 586 W/m², against 1361 W/m² at Earth [mars.solar.constant_mean] [sun.solar_constant_1au]. A typical night at Jezero also drops to about 193 K (−80 °C) [jezero.temperature.my36_air_diurnal_min]. So a solar-powered beacon would have to save daylight to glow after dark, and keep its electronics from freezing. Which would you like?
- **Solar-powered:** it reacts to rovers only during daylight hours, or it glows dimmer at night to save charge.
- **Always on:** you assume a power source we don't model (a buried line from your base, a mystery battery). The inspector will label that as your assumption.

**2. How should it stand out through the dust?** Even in the clear season, Jezero's sky has a dust optical depth of about 0.4 [jezero.dust.optical_depth_background_my36]. In the January 2022 regional storm it peaked around 2 [jezero.dust.optical_depth_storm_jan2022], enough to make distant lights fade into the haze. What should it look like?
- **Tall and bright:** a tall mast with a big light that's easy to spot from far off.
- **Small and local:** a low marker, since 20 m is close range anyway.
- **Signal as well as light:** it also broadcasts "rover near" so your other inventions (a gate, a siren, a friend's camp) can react even when nobody can see it.

The 20 m trigger distance is your design choice, and I'll keep it exactly as you said.

answer.name: rover_beacon

manifest.name: rover beacon
manifest.description: A tall mast with a big lamp that lights up bright amber while any rover is within 20 m, and broadcasts a 'rover near' signal (and the distance) every tick while one is, so gates, sirens or a neighbour's camp can react. Always on: its power source is the player's assumption.
manifest.author: design agent

state.label: distance to nearest rover (-1 = no rover)

emits.label: distance to the rover that is near

did_you_know.text: Even in Jezero's clear season the sky holds enough dust for a visible optical depth of about 0.4, and in the January 2022 regional storm it climbed to about 2. That is why this beacon stands tall and burns bright.

answer.explanation:
**What it does.** Your beacon is a 4 m mast with a dark lens on top and a little cap above it. Every tick it asks the world how far away the nearest rover is. When that rover is 20 m or closer, the lens is swapped for a big bright amber lamp. When the rover moves farther away, the lamp goes dark again.

While a rover is in range, the beacon broadcasts two signals every tick:
- **Signal 200:** the value 1, meaning "a rover is near".
- **Signal 201:** the rover's distance in metres.

Your other inventions can listen for these. A gate or a siren should check signal 200. Because the beacon re-sends it every tick, nothing misses it. The inspector shows the live distance (−1 if there is no rover) and whether the lamp is lit. The log notes each time the lamp switches on or off.

**Facts that shaped it.**
- **Dust:** Jezero's clear-season sky has a dust optical depth of about 0.4 [jezero.dust.optical_depth_background_my36], and the January 2022 storm pushed it to about 2 [jezero.dust.optical_depth_storm_jan2022]. That's why you chose tall and bright, and why the signal matters when nobody can see the lamp.
- **Power:** sunlight at Mars averages 586 W/m², against 1361 W/m² at Earth [mars.solar.constant_mean] [sun.solar_constant_1au], and nights drop to about 193 K [jezero.temperature.my36_air_diurnal_min]. So an always-on lamp is not something the world gives you for free.

**Your assumptions, not facts about Mars.**
- The beacon is always powered. You assumed the power source, and the world doesn't model it.
- The 20 m trigger distance is your choice.
- The 4 m mast height, the lamp sizes and the amber colour are my design choices for "tall and bright", not Mars numbers.
- Signal codes 200 and 201 are just labels we picked. Tell me if you'd like different ones to match a friend's camp.
